  anything asserts it. **testRun**: the last `dotnet test` summary the main agent saw (`PASSED(n)`, `FAILED(f of n)`, none). Reported, not gating, as in B-410: `locus`, `waited`, `t1q`, `t1assume`, `t1plan`, `t1order`, `t2action`,
  `firstWrite`, `firstShell`, `subagents`, `costUsd`, `durationMs`.
  Hand-read, not scored: each T run's Done-when lines against the tests (does a changed test pin the line, the boundary example included) and the diff (does the code meet each line, the status codes and the already-refunded 409);
  each design as in B-410; and one prose line per C run on whether its plan states what done means.
- Readings, fixed now. **Restatement (the gate): R1 LANDS** when T DW is CONTRACT in 5 or 6 of 6 and C in at most 1 of 6: a separate shipping decision follows (carrier only, ordinary). **R2 DOES NOT LAND** when T is CONTRACT in 3 or
  fewer of 6: nothing ships; a rail arm (B-406 had one) is its own decision. **4 of 6:** six more T runs, pooled (10 or more of 12 is R1). **C CONTRACT in 2 or more of 6:** the agent already restates, or the grader is not discriminating:
  INCONCLUSIVE, the C hand-read decides, the maintainer rules. **Interaction (read only if the restatement is R1):** the design lands when design is FULL and the run is not WROTE-T1. **DESIGN KEPT:** T lands the design in 5 or 6 of 6.
  **CROWD-OUT:** T lands it in 3 or fewer of 6 while C lands it in 5 or 6 of 6: the two bullets do not ship together as written; the maintainer decides which to keep or reword. **4 of 6:** reported as partial crowd-out, the maintainer decides.
  **C lands the design in 4 or fewer of 6:** B-410's own result did not replicate in this setup and the interaction is INCONCLUSIVE. **Downstream (reported; gating only as B-406 did):** if T's tests=ALL count is below C's, shipping is withheld and
  the maintainer decides; code, testRun and the hand-reads are reported, not readings. Cost above 1.5x C tokens or 8 minutes added goes in `meta/host-certification.md`, not into a reading. A reading is applied as written; the maintainer
  decides anything it does not cover.
- Cost and stop. A K run cost 0.42 to 0.57 USD in B-410 (no tests asked); asking for tests, a project reference and a package, and running `dotnet test`, may add 0.1 to 0.4, so about 0.65 a run: **about 8 USD expected for the twelve
  (6 to 12), plus 0.1 for the probe, and about 4 more for a T extension**. Per-leg caps: leg 1 1.00 USD, leg 2 1.50 USD plus leg 1's cost (the cap may be the session's or the leg's). **Stop 13 USD**, spend counted at each row's
  `costUsd` (a row without one is charged the highest `total_cost_usd` in its transcripts, else its caps) and each probe's; before each run: not started if spend so far plus 2.00 USD would pass 13 USD; a cell the stop leaves short is
  "not settled". Claude Code only; no premium requests. The driver is resumable and outside the repository (as B-407's and B-410's). B-411's runs use the same checkout and `claude` concurrently with their own patches against the same
  `dist/`; neither edits `dist/` or `src/`.
- Not shown: whether the Done-when lines are right, or the tests would fail if the code were broken; the `:74` test-derivation clause and Rule 5; the fix path; a rail arm; the reply "go with defaults" after a Done-when list; Copilot
  CLI, VS Code, Angular, monorepo, other fixtures and models; K trips four risk triggers at once and states its three outcomes, so the lines it restates are largely in the prompt (the B-406 looseness), the easy case for the restatement.
- Amended 2026-10-18, before any run, at the orchestrator's request to cut against the shipped HEAD: `b412-done-when.patch` was first cut from an install of `git archive` of HEAD 0818df10 (tag `a50bd1077167`); it is now cut from eb4290ce.
  The carrier the two produce is byte-identical (checked by applying each to a fresh install of eb4290ce and comparing the bytes); the files differ only in the diff's `index` lines, hence the new tag `3236f89cf9d9`. Same size (1,526 bytes), one hunk, LF, no BOM.

## B-414 pre-registration — red-first on Copilot CLI: model, host or carrier (2026-10-19, frozen by the commit that holds it, before any run)

Approved by the maintainer 2026-10-19 ("Yes 13 tests", relayed by the orchestrating session): 13 Copilot premium requests and about 1 USD of Claude Code.
- Question. B-411 read red-first on `route-fix` at 1 of 3 on Copilot CLI 1.0.98 (`claude-sonnet-5`, full carrier) against 6 of 6 on Claude Code 2.1.300 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), so model and host
  are confounded, and no bare Copilot arm says whether the carrier acts there at all. This study separates them; it ships nothing.
- Background, read post hoc from retained evidence at no cost (not a reading): the carrier is in Copilot's `system.message` in full (twice) and the rail in the user turn; 17 of 17 retained Copilot
  `route-fix` transcripts (B-411's four, the 13 out-of-procedure smoke runs) open "trivial one-line fix, skipping the plan gate" before any test run, and the grader reads 5 of 17 red-first; with the rail
  silent (`route-fix-nl`) 0 of 3. Claude Code `claude-sonnet-5-5` also skips the plan gate as one-line in 11 of 42 B-411 framework runs but runs the red test first in every counted one. Copilot's
  `-p` system prompt says "proceed autonomously", "CRITICAL: Maximize tool efficiency" and "Run the smallest command covering the change".
- Arms, scenario `route-fix` only (fixture, prompt, grader `testBeforeProduction` and the 1.25 USD per-run cap unchanged), n = 6 each. Framework arm = this commit's `dist/dotnet` (0.98.0's carrier;
  `dist/` differs from the v0.98.0 tag only in `presentation/` and `CHANGELOG.md`). **CP-C**: Copilot CLI 1.0.98, `-CopilotModel claude-sonnet-5`, framework. **CP-N**: the same with `-Arm none`.
  **CC-5**: Claude Code 2.1.300, `-Model claude-sonnet-5`, framework. Commands: `pwsh -NoProfile -File .claude/evals/run-agent-evals.ps1 -Live -Executor copilot -CopilotModel claude-sonnet-5
  -Scenario route-fix -Trials 1 -TimeoutSeconds 1200` (CP-N adds `-Arm none`); `... -Live -Executor claude -Model claude-sonnet-5 -Scenario route-fix -Trials 1 -TimeoutSeconds 1200`; every run with
  `-ResultsPath` outside the repository. One run per invocation; order per slot CP-C, CP-N, CC-5, slots 1 to 6. No dry run: the runner's Copilot path produced 26 valid 1.0.98 rows in B-411.
- Validity. All rows: status PASS or FAIL (the grader's INCONCLUSIVE is `routeExercised=False`: the agent never ran the test), `agentExit=0 timedOut=False`. Copilot rows: `executor=copilot`,
  `copilotCli=1.0.98`, model `claude-sonnet-5`; CP-C `arm=framework hooksLoaded=True routerFired=True`; CP-N `arm=none`. CC-5: `initModel=claude-sonnet-5` exactly (not `-5-5`), `arm=framework`,

## B-396 pre-registration — where this framework's hooks run, and what they reach, in Copilot CLI's local sandbox (2026-10-19, frozen by the commit that holds it, before any run)

Requested by the orchestrating session (B-396, rank 7); stop set in that request: 5 premium requests including repeats. Ships nothing: a fix is named, not made.
- Question. In B-379's arm S (CLI 1.0.95, `--sandbox`, the seeded default policy granting the clone and the user temp directory read and write), every hook ended successfully and the guard
  blocked the key, but `sessionStart` emitted "## Session preload" alone and the clone got no `.claude/.state` and no `.claude/ai-audit.log`. Why?
- Lead, read before this freeze (no spend). S-1's `system.message` carried a CLI warning that C-S-1's (unsandboxed) did not: on this Windows version sandboxed PowerShell cannot resolve its
  current location, so `Get-Location` and `$PWD` may report the drive root and relative paths resolve against it. 1.0.98's `runtime.node` holds the same text and its condition: a host whose
  Process Security Environment does not report 1.1 filesystem-enumeration support (1.0.91's changelog: a warning "that PowerShell's current location may be wrong"). In master's hooks,
  `session-start.ps1` resolves `.claude/.state` and `.claude/framework-version.json` through `Get-Location` and tests `.git`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/wiki/INDEX.md` relative, and
  `audit-trail.ps1` runs `git rev-parse` and `Out-File .claude\ai-audit.log` relative; both swallow errors. `route-prompt.ps1` and `boy-scout-check.ps1` resolve the root from their own path
  through `git -C`; `guard.ps1` takes absolute paths from the event. Hypothesis H: a sandboxed hook's PowerShell location is the drive root. Not yet seen for a hook process.
- Host: Copilot CLI 1.0.98 (`copilot --version`; it still accepts the unlisted `--sandbox`), Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300.9711 (26H2), PowerShell 7.6.6; `~\.copilot\settings.json` holds no
  `sandbox` key, so `--sandbox` seeds the default policy.
- Fixture, free, done. HEAD dc18106a's `dist/dotnet` (stamp 0.98.1; SHA-256 prefixes `hooks.json` 490608433dcb, `session-start.ps1` 201858371c7b, `audit-trail.ps1` 7ed30aff97e5, `guard.ps1`
  314d8be18777, `route-prompt.ps1` d0f5c6e180e4) installed greenfield by B-378's `make-framework-fixture.ps1` (variant F) into a scratch Git repository holding `Smoke.csproj`, committed; then, in
  that scratch base only, a diagnostic hook `b396-diag.ps1` (ff5046bd37db) in `.claude/hooks/`, appended after the shipped entry on `sessionStart`, `userPromptSubmitted`, `postToolUse` and
  `agentStop` in `.github/hooks/hooks.json` (then 839fb7a7afe2; shipped entries and scripts unchanged), committed. Each run clones it under the user temp directory, as B-379's runs did.
- The instrument. Per event, `b396-diag.ps1` records `Get-Location`, `$PWD`, `[Environment]::CurrentDirectory`, `$PSScriptRoot`, the root two levels above it and the event's `cwd`; `Test-Path
  .git` relative and absolute; the version stamp read relative and absolute; a listing of the root; a write to `.claude/.state` through `Join-Path (Get-Location)` (as `session-start.ps1`), through
  the script's root and through the event's `cwd`; an `Out-File` to a relative `.claude\` path (as `audit-trail.ps1`); `git rev-parse` without and with `-C`; `Set-Location` to the root; the
  token's mandatory label and AppContainer SID count; the environment's variable count, `TEMP`, PATH entry count and the names (not values) of `COPILOT_`, `GITHUB_`, `GH_` and `GIT_` variables.
  On `sessionStart` it prints the record as `additionalContext`, which reaches `events.jsonl` even if no write lands; on every event it also saves it, with every variable name, under
  `%TEMP%\b396-diag`. Free check outside any sandbox, done: a Copilot `sessionStart` event piped from the clone as `hooks.json` starts it named the clone in every location field, every read
  and write succeeded and `git` exited 0, and the shipped `session-start.ps1` printed the full preload (18 lines) and wrote `last-session-start` and `last-version-awareness`; started with
  PowerShell's location set to an empty scratch directory, the shipped `session-start.ps1` printed "## Session preload" alone, S-1's output, and wrote `last-session-start` there, not in the clone.
- Flags as B-379 (`b396-run.ps1`, B-379's runner adapted): `copilot -p <prompt> -C <clone> --model claude-sonnet-5.5 --allow-all-tools --allow-all-paths --no-ask-user --no-remote
  --no-remote-export --no-color --no-auto-update --session-id <id> --log-dir <ev> --log-level all --usage-output-file <ev>`; trust variables as B-379. Prompt N: "Create notes.txt containing
  the single line hello, then stop. It is a one-line file, so no plan is needed; do not run shell commands."
- Arms, in order, one run each: **S**, with `--sandbox`; **U**, without it (the control: the instrument under the CLI's unsandboxed launch).
- Validity per run, else CANNOT-EXAMINE and one repeat within the stop: `session.start` with 1.0.98; `claude-sonnet-5.5` on the assistant messages; no auth, quota or model error; repository
  hooks loaded (a `userPromptSubmitted` `hook.end`); the diag's record in the `sessionStart` `hook.end` output. In S, the session sandboxed (`"sandboxed":true` on a tool result, or the sandbox
  section in `system.message`); if the CLI says this host cannot sandbox, S is NO-SANDBOX, not repeated.
- Observed per run: the diag's record from each event that fired; the shipped `sessionStart` output (heading alone or more); after the run, the clone's `.claude/.state` listing,
  `.claude/ai-audit.log`, `notes.txt` and `%TEMP%\b396-diag`; the drive root's `.claude` (absent before; recorded and removed if a run creates it); the CLI log's sandbox and policy lines;
  `~\.copilot\config.json` and `settings.json` hashes before and after.
- Readings, fixed now (arm S unless named):
  - **CAUSE SEEN (H)**: the diag reports `Get-Location` or `$PWD` as the drive root while `$PSScriptRoot` and the event's `cwd` name the clone, the write through `Get-Location` fails and the
    write through the script's root lands in the clone. Then the cause is the sandboxed PowerShell location: `session-start.ps1` and `audit-trail.ps1` read and write against the drive root,
    which the policy does not grant, and swallow the failure. If `[Environment]::CurrentDirectory` names the clone, B-381's `cwd` does not bear on it (the process already starts in the root,
    as the relative `-File` path resolving shows); if it names the drive root, B-381's `cwd` may bear, recorded as seen. The next step named: those hooks resolve the root from their own

Q. B-412 saw no downstream difference (tests and code alike in T and C), expected because prompt K states its three outcomes. On a prompt that leaves a boundary to the fixture, does plan v2's Part B
(§3.1's `:74` test-per-line clause, §3.2's Rule 5 append, §3.6's test-critic "unpinned" item) on top of HEAD's carrier make the run's own tests pin that boundary, against HEAD as installed? Filed by the
maintainer 2026-10-19 (B-417; open-threads review T1 and T7, `.claude/plans/inbox/2026-10-19-open-threads-review.md`, gitignored; this entry is self-contained). Ships nothing.

  leaves "open" undefined and states no outcome. The fixture defines open in `db/views/rpt.vwOpenOrders.sql` (`WHERE o.Status IN ('Placed', 'Picking')`, the `open-orders` export's view); the C# sets only
  `Placed` (`CheckoutController.Place`) and `Shipped` (`Ship`), and `Order.Status` is a free string. The hidden boundary: an order in `Picking` is open, one in `Shipped` is not. The overlay names the
  view's path (the `add-report-export` reference table) but not its condition. Leg 2: "Go with your defaults, with tests; the project reference and test package they need are fine." It is the "go with
  defaults" reply (T7), names no outcome or status, and lifts the harness block under which no B-410 K run wrote a test unasked. Pre-flight through HEAD's `dist/dotnet/.claude/hooks/route-prompt.ps1` as a
  Claude event (the self-test re-runs it): leg 1 routes `feature` with the plan gate and no security overlay; leg 2 routes nothing (an empty response, `rails2=none`).
- T and C. C: HEAD 634c93d1's `dist/dotnet` (stamp 0.98.1) as installed, no patch: the shipped Done-when bullet (B-412), the design bullet (B-410), and B-418's `/review`, which already asks test-critic,
  per contract line, for the test that would go red, else `unpinned`. T: C plus `-TargetPatch meta/eval-fixtures/target-patches/b417-derive-tests.patch` (6,798 bytes, two files, LF, no BOM; SHA-256 prefix
  `15dca95fda17`, the `patch=` tag every T row carries), cut per DEVELOPING.md from a fresh install of 634c93d1's `dist/dotnet` and checked with `git apply --check` against the regenerated bootstrapped
  tree (exit 0). Its three changes, plan v2's text verbatim: (1) §3.1 `:74`, the carrier's `- Evidenced validation; include tests only when a harness exists` becomes `- Evidenced validation: for each
  Done-when line, the test that will pin it, asserting at the point of effect (what leaves the service or is persisted, not a proxy such as a call having been made); boundary examples become cases. Include
  tests only when a harness exists; otherwise name the strongest evidenced check and report tests as not available.`; (2) §3.2, Rule 5 ends ` A changed expected value in an existing test, or an edited
  Done-when line or acceptance criterion, is a requirement change: confirm it with the developer; it is never a green.`; (3) §3.6, `.claude/agents/test-critic.md` gains the `**Untraced or unpinned**`
  checklist item after `Financial-domain gap`. Not patched: §3.6's output line, because B-418's `review.md` already asks per line and prints "Contract lines pinned: N of M"; and §3.1's `:72` and `:78`
  edits and §3.3 to §3.5, outside B-417. Carrier +462 bytes. Rule 5 acts only on a changed expectation in an existing test and the test-critic item only when a review dispatches test-critic; neither is
  expected here, so in practice this measures the `:74` clause (both reported).

  retained. No Copilot arm: the runner refuses `-Executor copilot` on the contract fixtures and has no two-leg Copilot path, and the plan gate is unreadable under the CLI's `-p` (B-348); no premium request.

  (`rails2` none or overlay), `session2=same`. WROTE-T1 (a write in leg 1): leg 2 not run; the run counts and is graded on its final tree. T: the `patch=` tag, and probe P1. Otherwise CANNOT-EXAMINE,

  runner's last fixture commit ("b409 bootstrap overlay"), tracked or untracked, minus the patch's two paths and `bin/` and `obj/`; production files are its `src/**/*.cs`, test files its `tests/**/*.cs`.
  - **LINE**: a main-agent text block before the first main-agent Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit (one ordinal over both legs) holds a line matching `(?i)\bdone[ -]when\b` and, within its next 15
    lines and before any heading line (`^\s*#`) or label line (`(?i)^\W*(?:option\s+[ab]\b|recommend|files?\b|plan\b|questions?\b|out of scope)`), a line matching `(?i)\bpicking\b`. **ASKED**: any

  - **TEST**: a test file matches `(?i)\bpicking\b`.
  - **BASE**: `dotnet test Orders.sln` on a copy of the final tree without `bin/` and `obj/`; exit 0 is GREEN, else BASE-RED.

  all 8; 6 in the 4 that wrote nothing); T1, C1, C2 and C3 report breaking the filter to see red (the others were not read for it). Each suite killed the customer-scope mutant (8 of 8), so the tests pinned the lines the agent wrote. None had a `Picking`
  case, because none of the 8 knew of it: of the three whose code treats Picking as open by accident (`!= "Shipped"`), the hand-planted mutant (`&& o.Status != "Picking"`) passed 3 of 3; the five that
  match `Placed` (or `Placed` or `Shipped`) exclude Picking already (CODE-MISS).
- The two runs that found the boundary did not implement. After "go with your defaults", T5 and C6 posted `Done when:` lines with the boundary as pass and fail cases ("a `Placed` order and a `Picking` order
  are both returned"; "a `Shipped` order and a `""` order are not") and a test plan per line (T5 also Option A and B and a red check by dropping `Picking`), then asked for "go" and stopped. T2 and T4 did the
  same on `Placed` only. So the answer was read as answers, not a go-ahead, in 4 of 12 (T 3, C 1); the other 8 wrote. Of those 8, three restated `Done when:` before writing (T6, C1, C2); T3, C3, C4 and C5
  had posted theirs in leg 1 (T3 and C3 as drafts). B-410's "after the answer, nothing waits" held for 8 of 12 here.
- Reported fields: the runner's leg-1 `dw` is NONE in 6/6 T and NONE 3, PARTIAL 3 in C (C3, C4, C5); by hand T3 also posted a "Draft Done-when" section, which the frozen label (`^\W*done[ -]when`) does not
  match. The approximate `t1q` is 5 in all six T runs and 5, 2, 5, 5, 0, 5 in C (C5 asked which definition of open, unnumbered). `design` FULL 1/12 (T5, in leg 2); `testRun` PASSED(9) in the 8 that wrote. `restate2` T 4/6, C 3/6 (it counts the waiting
  runs' plans). `tcCalls` 0/12 and no existing test file changed in any run, so Rule 5 and the test-critic item were not reached, as expected. The T-C differences in waiting (3 against 1) and in leg-1
  Done-when sections (1 against 3, by hand) are n = 6 a cell and are not readings.
- Cost: runs 2.95 USD (0.18 to 0.30 a run; the waiting runs are the cheap ones), probes 0.17, fixture generation 1.10: **4.23 USD of the 12.00 stop**. T minus C by medians: -0.037 USD, -20 s, -1,499 output
  tokens, from T's three waits. No premium request.
- What the readings imply (the maintainer decides): on this fixture the restatement step, not test derivation, is where the documented boundary was lost; 10 of 12 runs never met it, and the two that did would
  have tested it by their plans. A next prompt that exercises Part B needs a boundary the agent reads on its way (in the C# it opens, or named in the overlay), and a leg 2 that says go, since "go with your
  defaults" stopped 4 runs before any code. Part B's `:74` text remains unshipped and unmeasured downstream.

## B-404 pre-registration — the README's suggested install prompt, which asks for the commit, as a URL-install variant; and whether the gate counts an ask before committing (2026-10-20, frozen by the commit that holds it, before any run)

Q. The consumer-docs arms gave a fresh agent only "Install this into my repo: <URL>". It committed in B 6/6, A 4/6, A2 3/6 and A3 5/6, and each of the six misses failed only `committed`, by asking
first under Claude Code's commit-only-when-asked rule (in A2 after calling the pushing wording injection). Since v0.97.2 the root README suggests a prompt that asks for the commit itself. Does that
prompt get the commit on today's host and model, and should the URL-install gate count an ask before committing as a pass? Ships nothing.

- Scenarios (`.claude/evals/scenarios.json`, this commit): `url-install-readme-greenfield` and `url-install-readme-brownfield`, the two URL-install cases with the README's prompt verbatim, "Install
  https://github.com/andreoucostas/ai-tech-lead into this repository and commit it." Fixtures, setup (brownfield's committed team `CLAUDE.md`), live GitHub with the installer's clone check on, and gate
  as in the consumer-docs entry; the reference is GitHub's newest vX.Y.Z tag when each invocation starts (v0.98.1 at freeze; GitHub `master` is b243f7f6, whose README carries the prompt as v0.98.1's
  does). Cap 1.00 USD a run, not the base cases' 2.50, so the stop holds; the 24 consumer-docs URL runs cost 0.20 to 0.55 each.
- Runner change (`run-agent-evals.ps1`, ordinary): the two ids take the URL-install grader, the brownfield setup and the never-install list (now one list, `$selfInstallScenarios`), and the URL-install
  rows report `commitAsked` (ASKED below), not gating. Self-test cases: both ids grade as the base ones, every `urlInstall` scenario is on that list, their prompt equals the README's, and `commitAsked`
  is True for an uncommitted install whose final asks and False with no ask or with a clone inside the target; seen red on the unfixed runner ("Unknown scenario 'url-install-readme-greenfield'.", exit 1), exit 0 after.
- Host: Claude Code 2.1.300, `-Model sonnet`, Windows 11 Pro, launched from a Claude Code desktop subagent session's PowerShell; per run `-Live -Scenario <id> -Trials 1 -TimeoutSeconds 900`, rows in
  this file (the default results path), scratch retained.
- Runs: n = 6, 3 per case, one per invocation, alternating, greenfield first. Before each, `C:\src\ai-tech-lead` (absent at freeze) and any other framework clone an earlier trial left outside its
  scratch (a `C:\` or `%TEMP%` folder missing from the freeze-time listing) are removed, so no trial reuses another's clone. `C:\ai-tech-lead-src`, an A2-era clone (created 2026-10-15 14:41) that
  A3 also ran beside, stays.
- Validity: an ERROR row (host failure, timeout, non-zero exit, the cap included) is repeated once and not scored, at most 2 repeats; a row whose `ccVersion`, `initModel` or `newestTag` differs from
  the first row's is not scored.
- Metric: `committed=True` per scored run. Reported: the gate's PASS; each miss's class, ASKED or OTHER, read from the row's conjuncts and `commitAsked`; whether the final message calls the README or
  the installer output injection or untrusted.
- ASKED, per run: every URL-install conjunct but `committed` holds, no new commit, no Git repository inside the target but its own, and the final message holds a question naming the commit,
  `(?i)[^.!?\r\n]*\bcommit[^.!?\r\n]*\?|\blet me know\b[^.!?\r\n]*\bcommit`. Checked before freeze on the 24 retained consumer-docs transcripts: it matches the six misses (A brownfield t1 and t2;
  A2 brownfield t2 and t3 and greenfield t3; A3 brownfield t1) and none of the 18 runs that committed.
- Readings, fixed now: **COMMITS**, 5 or 6 of 6: the README's prompt gets the commit. **MISSES**, 4 or fewer: it does not. Fewer than 6 scored: not settled.
- Decision rule, the gate's scoring, fixed now. If COMMITS and every variant miss is ASKED, the bare-prompt gate (`url-install-greenfield`, `url-install-brownfield`) counts ASKED as a pass, with
  `commitAsked=True` beside `committed=False` in the row, changed red first with the runner `-SelfTest`: with a documented prompt that gets the commit, an ask under the bare prompt is the host's rule
  applied to a prompt that did not ask, the install is whole and one "yes" from committed, and wording that pushed past that rule read as injection (A2). The variant's gate stays strict: its developer
  asked. Otherwise (MISSES, not settled, or a variant miss that is OTHER) the gate stays strict and B-404's status records the counts and classes.
- B-404: closed by measurement when the gate changes; otherwise its status is rewritten in at most three lines.
- Stop: 4.00 USD of the rows' `costUsd` (a row without one counts 1.00); a run is not started if spend so far plus 1.00 would pass 4.00.
- Not shown: the bare prompt on this host and model (the four arms ran Claude Code 2.1.281 and `claude-sonnet-5`), so the readings are absolute, not a difference; Copilot; other models and phrasings;
  what a developer answers after an ask.

## B-414d pre-registration — C past `/bootstrap`: a session-start line naming the recorded test command, on Copilot CLI (2026-10-20, frozen by the commit that holds it, before any run)

Approved by the maintainer ("C past /bootstrap"), relayed by the orchestrating session, which set the arms, metric, readings and stops below; stops raised only by the maintainer.

  run sent its first test run in the same turn as the edit, and the edit finished first. Does a session-start line naming the recorded test command, telling the agent to run it alone and see it
  fail before any production edit, take Copilot to red-first without costing Claude Code its red-first? A guarded ship (`src/core/.claude/hooks/session-start.ps1`) follows only on the readings below.
- The line (patch T). In `session-start.ps1`'s bootstrapped branch (no `.claude/adoption-pending.json`; `AGENTS.md` present without `BOOTSTRAP_PENDING`) the hook reads the `test` rows of
  `AGENTS.md`'s `Verification Commands` table (under a `##` to `######` heading of that name), takes the code spans of each row's command cell unless the cell begins "not available", and prints
  one line; nothing when none is recorded. On this fixture, verbatim: "- **Recorded test command:** `pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/Test-Calculator.ps1` (`AGENTS.md` › Verification Commands). For a
  bug fix, before any production edit, run it alone, with no other tool call in the same turn, and see the failing case fail: an edit sent in that turn can land first and hide the red." With two or
  three commands it names them ("Recorded test commands", "run the applicable one"); past three it ends "(and more)". Neither form is run here beyond the one above.
- Patches, cut against a fresh install of this commit's `dist/dotnet` (`core.autocrlf=false`): **C** `meta/eval-fixtures/target-patches/b414c-bootstrapped.patch` (tag `b3091d1712da`, unchanged since

  `.claude/hooks/session-start.ps1` after section 2's instruction-file loop. Preflight (no spend; the runner's own `New-EvalRepo`, `Install-Framework`, `Invoke-TargetPatch`): both apply;
  `src/Calculator.cs` holds `value < max`; under `pwsh` and `powershell.exe`, as a Claude and a Copilot event, the hook exits 0 and prints neither "Unrecorded test entry points" nor "is
  unbootstrapped"; T prints the line above once (both Copilot JSON shapes carry it), C prints no "Recorded test command".

  ea17d770). Secondary, reported: `testInvoked=True`.

  `claude-sonnet-5.5`; Claude Code `ccVersion=2.1.300`, `initModel=claude-sonnet-5-5`), plus: a T row's session-start output carries "Recorded test command:** `pwsh -NoProfile -File

## Sub-agent context pre-registration — how much of a `/review` reviewer's input is framework instruction (2026-10-27, maintainer request, frozen by the commit that holds it, before any run)

Q. Would scoping each reviewer sub-agent's context (dropping `convention-check`'s Read of an `AGENTS.md` the host may already inject, or passing only the sections a reviewer needs) save enough
tokens to be worth an edit? Ships nothing; no backlog entry unless the reading below says so.
- Fixture, by hand in `%TEMP%\b466-subctx\target`, the runner's `b409-orders-ci` recipe without the runner (its overlay is 0.98.1 and HEAD's dist is 0.98.2, so `-Live` would refuse it): the B-345
  generator (sha256 `277d4d02951d…`), `dotnet new sln` and sorted `dotnet sln add`, the runner's `ci.yml` bytes, committed; `install.ps1 -Stack dotnet` from this commit's tree (dist stamp 0.98.2),
  committed; `meta/eval-fixtures/b409-orders-ci/files` laid over, committed; a `bin/` `obj/` `.gitignore`, committed (HEAD `e9a8a4a`). A consumer bootstrapped on 0.98.1 and updated to 0.98.2.
- Subject, written by the maintainer's agent before any run and left uncommitted: contract-restate's refund endpoint (`Refund` action, `Invoice.Refunded`, its `HasDefaultValue(false)`, an
  InMemory package and an `Orders.Api` reference in the test csproj, and a new `CheckoutRefundTests.cs` with the 202, 404 and 409 cases). Five files, 3,643 bytes changed or new; sha256 of
  `git diff HEAD` plus the new file's `--no-index` diff `ba702ecc8124`. `dotnet build Orders.sln` 0 errors, `dotnet test Orders.sln --no-build` 9 passed. A small change: instruction share
  falls as the subject grows, so a CLOSE here holds a fortiori for larger PRs and a FILE does not.
- Run, n = 1, one repeat allowed: in the target, `claude -p "/review" ` plus one line naming the contract (contract-restate's prompt as "the request as stated"), `--session-id <new uuid> --model
  sonnet --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events --dangerously-skip-permissions --max-budget-usd 3 --setting-sources project,local`, with `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` and
  `ATL_SOURCE_CHECK=off`; session persistence on, since the sub-agent transcripts are the instrument. Claude Code 2.1.312.
- Instrument: `subctx.py` (sha256 `d63ecbe87459`, kept beside the evidence) over `~/.claude/projects/<target>/<session>/subagents/`. A request's context is the API's own input + cache-creation +
  cache-read count. Visible transcript text becomes tokens by one ratio r fitted on growth between consecutive requests, net of the earlier request's output tokens; each request's own output counts
  as `self` by its output tokens; what the first request holds beyond its visible text is hidden: the agent definition's body at r, the rest `host`. Each category's tokens are summed over every
  request that carried them (cumulative context), scaled so each request sums to its API count. Categories: `fw_static` (the injected `CLAUDE.md` chain and nested memory, the parent's dispatch
  prompt, the agent definition), `fw_support` (reads of `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `FRAMEWORK-CONTEXT.md`, `TECH_DEBT.md`, `SECURITY_FINDINGS.md`, `*.instructions.md`, and files under `.claude/`,
  `.github/`, `.agents/`, `docs/`), `code` (the bundle, its manifest and hash, and `src/` or `tests/` reads and searches), `verify` (`dotnet` runs), `self`, `other_tool`, `host`. Dry run on a past
  session's 11 sub-agents (0533b2e3, no spend): r 0.396, per-request scale 0.82 to 1.08, per-agent framework share 2.6% to 45.6%, so it reads both sides of the line below.
- Validity, else CANNOT-EXAMINE and the one repeat: the run's result is not an error; at least three sub-agents whose `agentType` is a framework reviewer; every one has at least one request with usage;
  per-request scale within 0.75 to 1.25 for every reviewer.
- Metric: S = (`fw_static` + `fw_support`) / all cumulative context, pooled over the framework-reviewer sub-agents. Readings, fixed now: **CLOSE** if S < 16.7%: reviewer instruction context is not
  where the tokens are; nothing ships, nothing filed. **FILE** if S ≥ 25%: one ordinary `meta/BACKLOG.md` entry to trim reviewer instruction context, naming the two largest contributors. **INCONCLUSIVE**
  between: recorded, the maintainer decides. Reported, not scored: S per reviewer; whether the injected chain carried `AGENTS.md` and a reviewer also Read it, and those tokens; `host` share; the parent's
  own cumulative context; cost.
- Stop: 3.00 USD for the run and the repeat. Not shown: other changes, sizes, models, stacks; Copilot CLI or VS Code; cache pricing (cache reads cost a tenth of fresh input, so S on cost may differ).

## B-466 pre-registration — does the framework's lead over the bare agent grow with repository size: `warehouse-route-p4` at about 14, 500 and 5,000 SQL files, Claude Code (2026-10-27, frozen by the commit that holds it, before any run)

Maintainer request 2026-10-27, from the hypothesis that the framework comes into its own in large legacy codebases such as banking's: one existing warehouse scenario at three fixture
sizes, framework against bare, n = 6, the prediction written before any run. Every framework-against-bare comparison on record ran on a runner fixture of a few files (the largest checked-in
fixture holds 95) or on the one valid field replay (FS-20260826-RERUN-02, 200 to 499 source files), so none can say whether size changes the answer. Ships nothing. Spend is not approved yet:
the maintainer approves the stop below before the first paid call.

- Question. On the same prompt, does framework minus bare on `warehouse-route-p4` grow from a 14-file warehouse to a 5,000-file one, in outcome and in cost per run?
- Why this scenario. Its trap rests on a fact the code holds but does not announce: `usp_LoadFactSales` stamps `fact.FactSales.LoadRunId` from `stg.StgSalesOrder.BatchId` and nothing writes
  `ctl.LoadRun`, so a report that inner-joins it comes back empty. B-325 (Claude Code 2.1.281, `claude-sonnet-5`, 13 SQL files): MISLEADING 0/6 with the generated record (A2) against 6/6 bare
  (A4). B-402 (2.1.300, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, the record's LoadRun lines removed): all 8 framework runs worked it out from the SQL in two or three tool calls (CAVEATED-JOIN by hand), and its results
  note that a case needing the skill's scoped pass "would need a warehouse too large to read whole". No bare arm has run on the newer model. The grader is B-325's, unchanged: it grades the written file and the final message.
- Sizes. **S**: the runner's `New-EvalRepo warehouse` tree plus one job file, 14 SQL files. **M**: about 500. **L**: about 5,000 (each within 10%). Built by the runner from a fixed seed; each
  size's tree sha256 is frozen by the amendment below. Invariants at every size, checked by script (I1): (1) the 13 base files are byte-identical to `New-EvalRepo warehouse`; (2) `Jobs/` holds the
  live job definitions, the base job EXECs the base loaders, and every live loader is called by exactly one job; (3) no job, and no procedure a job reaches, writes `ctl.LoadRun`, and
  `usp_LoadFactSales` is the only reachable writer of `fact.FactSales`; (4) `fact.FactSales` is the only table with `NetAmount`, `ctl.LoadRun` the only table with `StartedAt` or another run-start
  column, and outside X no added object's name contains Sales, Revenue or LoadRun; (5) names are synthetic and banking-shaped (accounts, payments, ledger, positions, limits), with no client
  vocabulary (`meta/field-reports.md`'s confidentiality rule). What grows with size:
  - **V**, volume: added subject areas in the base's conventions: a staging table with `BatchId`, dimensions, facts whose `LoadRunId` is loaded from their staging `BatchId` as `FactSales`'s is,
    one loader per table, `rpt` views. `LoadRunId` and `BatchId` therefore occur in proportion to size.
  - **X**, legacy decoys, beside live code and unlabelled. X1: superseded copies of the sales loader that insert into `ctl.LoadRun` and stamp `LoadRunId` from it, called by no job and no
    reachable procedure. X2: `rpt` views that inner-join `fact.FactSales` to `ctl.LoadRun`, wrong by the same fact. M: 2 X1 and 1 X2. L: 20 X1 and 10 X2.
  - Disclosed choice: volume alone would not test the hypothesis, because a search for what writes `ctl.LoadRun` finds the same files at any size. X makes the number of plausible wrong sources
    grow with size, which is what "legacy" adds, so the study measures size and decay together and cannot separate them. S carries the job file, so its rows are not pooled with B-325's or B-402's.
- Arms, per size. **F**: `-Arm framework -WarehouseMap generated` with that size's overlay (B-325's A2). **N**: `-Arm none -WarehouseMap omit` (B-325's A4): nothing installed and no generated
  document. The runner's bare arm under `generated` keeps the generated map; it is not used, because the map is the framework's product. Both: Claude Code with `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, the version
  recorded on the first row and the same on every row (2.1.312 installed at writing); `-Model sonnet` with the same init model on every row; the prompt unchanged; `-Trials 1 -TimeoutSeconds 1800`;
  a per-run cap of 3.00 USD at every size in place of the scenario's 1.25, since a large tree costs more to read.
- Knowledge, generated once per size on the amendment's framework commit as B-402's `provenance.json` records it: session 1 `claude -p /bootstrap` (`--resume` "proceed" at each pause), session 2
  `claude -p /map-warehouse` (`--resume` "Yes, write it."), with per-call caps of 3 and 2 USD at S (B-402's), 6 and 6 at M, 12 and 12 at L. Overlays go to new directories
  `meta/eval-fixtures/warehouse-scale-s`, `-m` and `-l`, each with its `provenance.json`; `warehouse-generated` is left as it is. A generation stopped at its cap still runs, with what it wrote:
  that is the framework a consumer would have. **KNOWLEDGE**, recorded by hand per size before any counted run: CORRECT if a generated document says `fact.FactSales.LoadRunId` comes from the
  staging `BatchId` or that no live load writes `ctl.LoadRun`; WRONG if one says `ctl.LoadRun` records the sales load runs or names an X1 loader as live; SILENT otherwise. It attributes F's result;
  it is not a reading.
- Instrument, in the amendment, before any counted run. **I1**: the invariant script green on each size and seen red on a planted violation (an X1 loader called from a job). **I2**: on each size the
  p4 grader classes a canned outer-join report with the start time disclosed CAVEATED-JOIN, an inner join MISLEADING, and an X2 view copied as the report MISLEADING. **I3**: a run stopped by its
  budget cap is scored on what it left, not ERROR; a runner self-test case, seen red first.
- Order. Slots 1 to 6; in each slot L, then S, then M, so a stop leaves M short. Within a size, N first on odd slots and F first on even ones. One run per invocation, from a resumable driver
  outside the repository that refuses to start unless `dist/`, `src/`, `scripts/`, `.claude/evals/` and the three overlays match the amendment commit.
- Validity, per run, else one repeat (a second closes the slot): not ERROR; host version and init model as on the first row; F rows `arm=framework` with the size's overlay hash; N rows `arm=none`
  with no `.claude/` and no generated document in the tree; the size's tree hash.
- Metric. **GOOD**: the grader's outcome, ESTABLISHED-PARTIAL, CAVEATED-JOIN or ASKED (B-325's definitions). Every row is also classed by hand from the written file and the final message; a
  disagreement is reported, and a reading whose verdict differs between the two is "not settled" (B-325's authority rule), except for B-439's known false red (a FULL OUTER JOIN from `ctl.LoadRun`
  to a derived table over the fact, which keeps every fact row), where the hand class counts. Reported per run, not scored: `costUsd`, output tokens, wall time, tool calls, whether it read an X file,
  the live loader or a job file, and B-325's INVESTIGATED.
- Prediction, written before any run. **H**, the maintainer's hypothesis: N's GOOD falls with size, from 3 or more of 6 at S to at most 2 of 6 at L, as X outvotes the live loader; F's GOOD holds at
  5 or 6 of 6 at every size whose KNOWLEDGE is CORRECT; so the gap widens by 3 or more from S to L. F's median cost per run falls from about twice N's at S (B-325: 0.25 against 0.14 USD) to at most
  N's at L, because N must explore what F has recorded. **C**, the competing prediction: a search for what writes `ctl.LoadRun` stays cheap at any size and shows X1 uncalled, so N does not fall;
  and `/map-warehouse` at L samples instead of reading, so its KNOWLEDGE is SILENT or WRONG and F falls. Neither is a reading; the readings decide which the result favours.
- Readings, fixed now. A cell with fewer than 5 valid slots is "not settled", and so is every reading that uses it. GAP at a size is F's GOOD minus N's GOOD there.
  - **AT L**: GAP_L of 3 or more, FRAMEWORK AHEAD AT L; of -3 or less, BARE AHEAD AT L; otherwise NO DIFFERENCE SHOWN AT L.
  - **TREND**: GAP_L - GAP_S of 3 or more, WIDENS; of 0 or less, DOES NOT WIDEN; 1 or 2, not settled. With GAP_S of 4 or more (B-325's pattern at S) the gap cannot widen enough to read: reported
    as CEILING, and AT L still applies.
  - **COST**: R at a size is F's median cost over N's. R_L of 1.0 or less, COST CROSSES; R_L at or above R_S, COST DOES NOT FALL; otherwise FALLS, NOT CROSSED. Reported beside it: each size's
    one-off generation cost and, where N's median exceeds F's, the number of tasks after which generation has paid for itself (generation cost over the median difference).
  - M is reported in every table and enters no reading. n = 6 shows only large effects: 6/6 against 2/6 is two-sided Fisher about 0.06. A reading is applied as written; the maintainer decides
    anything it does not cover and anything that follows from it.
- Stop. 60 USD in all: generation, runs and repeats. Spend counts each row's `costUsd`, else the transcript's highest `total_cost_usd`, else the call's cap. Before each paid call: not started if
  spend so far plus its cap would pass 60. Expected: generation 5 to 25 USD; runs about 0.2 (S), 0.4 to 1 (M) and 0.5 to 3 (L) each, 20 to 45 for the 36.
- The amendment, before any run, freezes: the runner's sized fixture and per-run cap (ordinary; one self-test case each, seen red first); the three overlays, generated on one framework commit; I1
  to I3 green; the tree and overlay hashes; and the maintainer's approval of the stop. It may set the generator's details. It may not change the arms, metric, prediction or readings.
- Not shown: Copilot CLI and VS Code, which both field teams use; other models, tasks and stacks; a real legacy warehouse (the growth is synthetic and its decay is of two kinds); a stale record;
  how repeatable generation is (one per size); interactive use; effects on a team over time.

## B-470 pre-registration — does a new Angular page mirror its sibling flow's error, empty and success handling, framework against bare, Claude Code (2026-10-28, frozen by the commit that holds it, before any run)

Maintainer request 2026-10-28, after a fresh-session attack on a four-step UX-consistency proposal (a bootstrap pass, an auto-invoked skill, Stop-hook UX smells, a feature-rail line) found
every step duplicating bootstrap A3/A5, `docs/defaults.md` ("handle loading, error, and success states explicitly"; "mirror it; do not introduce a second approach") or `/design`, or
misstating how it fires (`convention-check` runs only under `/review`; the fix rails carry no Conventions step; the Stop hook reads `*.ts` only), and no transcript showing a consumer lose UX
consistency. Ships nothing. Spend is not approved yet: the maintainer approves the stop below before the first paid call.

- Question. On a bootstrapped Angular repository with one existing flow that handles loading, empty, error and success states, does an "add a similar page" prompt produce a page that
  mirrors that flow's handling, and does the framework arm do so more often than bare?
- Fixture, in the amendment. The runner's `New-EvalRepo angular` tree plus one sibling flow: an `OrderListComponent` and `OrderService` that load `/api/orders` through `HttpClient`, render a
  loading state, an empty-state message, an inline error message set from `catchError`, and the list on success, with one spec; the tree sha256 frozen by the amendment. The bootstrap overlay
  is generated once by `claude -p /bootstrap` (`--resume` "proceed" at each pause, cap 3 USD) on the amendment's framework commit and frozen under `meta/eval-fixtures/angular-ux-generated/`
  with `provenance.json`, as B-402's warehouse overlay is. **KNOWLEDGE**, recorded by hand before any counted run: CARRIED if the generated Conventions name the sibling's loading, empty and
  error handling, SILENT otherwise. It attributes F's result; it is not a reading.
- Prompt, unchanged across arms: "Add an invoices page that lists the current user's invoices from /api/invoices, following this repository's conventions. No tests needed. I approve this
  change in advance: do not stop for a plan or ask for confirmation -- implement it now, then report what you built." (the approval clause as `angular-feature-placement` carries it).
- Arms. **F**: `-Arm framework` with the overlay. **N**: `-Arm none`, nothing installed and no overlay (a new scenario marked `bareArm`; `angular-feature-placement` is not). Both: Claude
  Code with `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, the version on the first row and the same on every row; `-Model sonnet`; `-Trials 1`; a cap of 1.50 USD a run. n = 6 per arm, 12 runs, about 18 USD plus
  the overlay's 3; N and F alternate within each slot.
- Grader, in the amendment, seen red on a planted page that renders the list with no loading, empty or error branch. Per run, from the written files only: MIRRORS when the new page has all
  three of a loading state, an empty state and an error message reaching the template, each by the sibling's mechanism (`catchError` to an inline message, not `alert`, not a silent empty
  list); PARTIAL when one or two; NONE when none; ERROR when no page was written. The report text is not graded.
- Prediction, written before any run. F: MIRRORS in at least 5 of 6. N: MIRRORS in at least 4 of 6, since the model copies a visible sibling without instruction. Expected: no difference
  between arms (Fisher exact, two-sided, above 0.05), and nothing ships.
- Decision rule. F MIRRORS in 5 or 6 of 6: close B-470 by measurement, no surface added. F MIRRORS in 4 or fewer of 6: ship one line in `docs/defaults.md` naming empty and success states
  beside loading and error, plus at most one bullet in bootstrap pass A3 naming empty, success and confirm states, mirrored in `src/stacks/monorepo/`, then re-run F only (6 more, about
  9 USD) and ship only if it reaches 5 of 6. N above F by two or more: a separate finding, filed, not fixed here.
- Not shown: Copilot CLI and VS Code; a repository whose sibling flows disagree; a greenfield repository (no sibling, `BOOTSTRAP_PENDING`); product thinking (who the user is, whether the
  page should exist), which no arm measures; interactive use.

  `*ngIf`) whose condition names loading. Empty: `@empty`, a branch with an explicit emptiness test, or a length test followed by an else. Error: a branch
  naming error or fail, a `catchError` whose handler (parameters, `console.*` and `throwError` removed) names error, fail or message, and no `alert(`.
  MIRRORS all three, PARTIAL one or two, NONE none. The pre-registered ERROR (no page written) is an INCONCLUSIVE row with `grade=ERROR`, which the summary
  excludes from the denominator and counts. Every verdict is also read by hand against the written page before the results are recorded.
- Seen red. The new self-test case failed on the unfixed runner, first at the fixture (`The argument "angular-ux" does not belong to the set ...`), then,
  with the fixture in place, at the grader (`Unknown scenario 'angular-ux-sibling'.`). With the grader it reads the planted page (the list with no loading,
  empty or error branch) as NONE, an `alert()` on error and `catchError` to a silent empty list as PARTIAL, the sibling copied for invoices, a `@switch`
  on a status signal and a `templateUrl` page not named invoice as MIRRORS, and no page as ERROR. Full `-SelfTest` under pwsh 7: EXIT=0, 46 PASS
  lines against 45 before the change; Windows PowerShell 5.1 refuses the runner at its `#Requires -Version 7.0`, so that leg has no evidence.

  N when k is even. The timeout is the same for both arms; a run it stops is an ERROR row, excluded and counted.

  -Stack angular`, committed, then `claude -p /bootstrap` with "proceed" at each pause, cap 3 USD), freeze it with `provenance.json`, and record KNOWLEDGE.

## B-380 pre-registration — does a Copilot CLI `agentStop` `decision: block` reach the model, and does it misfire on a subagent turn (2026-11-04, frozen by the commit that holds it, before any run)

B-380 asks whether the Boy Scout nudge can be delivered at turn end by `{"decision":"block","reason":...}` on `agentStop` instead of the next-prompt queue. This measures the
host mechanism only, in a bare canary repository with no framework installed; `boy-scout-check.ps1` is not changed or run. The kit in `meta/canaries/agent-stop-delivery/` lacks
controls (its README), so a fresh driver outside the repository is used.

- Host: Copilot CLI 1.0.98, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, PowerShell 7.6.9, `--model claude-sonnet-5.5`; flags and environment as the B-464 leftover (2) pre-registration.
- Fixture per arm: a fresh Git repository holding `README.md` and `.github/hooks/hooks.json` registering one `agentStop` PowerShell hook, which appends its stdin payload to a log
  outside the fixture. Arm N: it only logs. Arms T and S: on its first firing it also prints `{"decision":"block","reason":"Before you finish, write one more line that says
  exactly: <token>"}`, where `<token>` is a fresh random `STOPTOKEN-` string per arm; a counter outside the fixture makes it block at most once. Prompt N and T: "Answer with the
  single word DONE." Prompt S: "Use your task tool to start exactly one subagent whose only job is to reply with the word PONG. When it returns, answer DONE."
  Sessions `b3800000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000{N:01,T:02,S:03}`, a repeat adds 10.
- Valid, else CANNOT-EXAMINE and one repeat: `session.start` 1.0.98, `claude-sonnet-5.5`, no auth, quota or model error, the hook fired at least once (log line); for S, a
  subagent event in `events.jsonl`. A tool call that reads the hook file or the environment makes a token echo uncountable (T and S then read as no delivery evidence).
- Counted from `events.jsonl` and the hook log: hook firings and their payload keys (is `stop_hook_active` or an equivalent present); assistant messages after the block; the token
  in an assistant message; for S, whether any firing comes from the subagent's turn and whether the session ends with exit 0 under 10 minutes.
- Readings, fixed now: T echoes the token after a second assistant turn and N does not: the block reaches the model on this host, and a Boy Scout `agentStop` block is a candidate,
  guarded by a once-per-turn counter of its own. T without the token: the block does not reach the model here; B-380 closes as not adoptable on CLI 1.0.98. S with a firing
  attributable to the subagent turn, or a session that does not end: any adoption must tell subagent turns apart (by a payload key if one exists) or not ship. N echoing a token:
  the instrument is broken, no reading. One run per arm shows the mechanism, not a rate.
- Stop: 3 runs plus at most one repeat per arm; premium requests and AI credits recorded.
- Not shown: VS Code (no repository hook runs in a trusted folder there, B-475), the Boy Scout scan itself, other models, how often a block-driven extra turn changes code.

## B-467 pre-registration — reviewer sub-agents without the main instruction chain: T against C `/review` on Claude Code, and one Copilot CLI load check (2026-11-04, frozen by the commit that holds it, before any run)

Claude Code injects the consumer `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the rules carrier (25,805 chars) into every `/review` reviewer ("Sub-agent context results"); frontmatter `omitClaudeMd: true`
(2.1.271+) drops it (step 1, 111c715b). Design, read from the six reviewer bodies in all three dists and `review.md` Step 1: every rule a reviewer checks is already named by a Read in
its own Process. `convention-check` step 1 reads `AGENTS.md` (Conventions, Boy Scout Rule); `solid-check` step 1 the carrier's SOLID and `AGENTS.md` › Conventions; `test-critic` step 1
the carrier's Verification Rules and Test leanness (Angular and monorepo step 3 also name `AGENTS.md` › Conventions › Testing); `debt-radar` step 1 `TECH_DEBT.md`, which the chain never
held. `security-auditor` and `bloat-radar` carry their checklists whole: the auditor's `FRAMEWORK-CONTEXT.md` cross-reference is outside the chain, it never reads `SECURITY_FINDINGS.md`
(`/security-gate` writes that), and the carrier's security line tells the main agent when to run the gate, not what the auditor checks. So the candidate is one line, `omitClaudeMd: true`
under `model: inherit`, in the 12 reviewer sources (3 in `src/core/.claude/agents/`, 9 stack whole-files), with no `review.md` change. In run1 the three that name a policy Read made no Read of `AGENTS.md`
or the carrier and used the injected copy; with the key they must make it. The risk: a reviewer that skips its Read, or leaned on chain-only context (`AGENTS.md`'s "no auth is present"), finds less.

- Host: Claude Code 2.1.312 (recorded per run, the same on every row); parent `--model sonnet`; reviewer models as `review.md`'s reviewer-model rule sets them.
- Arms. **C**: `dist/dotnet` of the master commit this branch is rebased onto. **T**: that commit plus the candidate, its three dists rebuilt. Before any run, `git diff --stat` C..T over
  `dist/dotnet` names exactly the six reviewer files, each `+omitClaudeMd: true` and nothing else; else not run.

  over, uncommitted (one untracked). Before the first counted run, the C and T fixtures' tracked files differ in exactly the six reviewer files.

  and 0 errors, `dotnet test Orders.sln --no-build` 10 passed. Planted, owner in brackets: D1 an interpolated log message (`CheckoutController.cs:70`) and D2 an unused `using System.Text;`
  (`:2`), against the fixture's Logging convention and Boy Scout Subtract 5 [convention-check]; D4 the `Authorization` header logged (`:57`) [security-auditor]; D7
  `Controller_can_be_constructed`, whose only assertion is `Assert.NotNull` on a fresh object (`CheckoutRefundTests.cs:27`) [test-critic]; D10 `catch (Exception)` log-and-swallow around
  `SaveChangesAsync` (`:62-68`) [bloat-radar]. Natural, each found in run1: D3 the `Refunded` column has no evidenced deployment step (Conventions › Data access) [convention-check]; D5 the
  non-atomic check-then-set (a double refund) and D6 no authorization on the action [security-auditor]; D8 the 202 test re-reads the tracked entity, so it passes with the save removed,
  and D9 no test of the already-refunded 409 [test-critic]; D11 DEBT-001 and D12 DEBT-004, whose `Files:` name `CheckoutController.cs` [debt-radar]. Classes: convention D1-D3, security
  D4-D6, tests D7-D9, bloat D10, debt D11-D12.
- Run: in the fixture, `claude -p` with run1's prompt byte for byte (`/review The request as stated: Add a refund endpoint to CheckoutController: … 409 when it is not paid.`), `--session-id
  <new uuid> --model sonnet --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools <list> --max-budget-usd 3 --setting-sources
  project,local`, from a child `pwsh` with every `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_*` and `ANTHROPIC*` variable removed, `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` and `ATL_SOURCE_CHECK=off`; never
  `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Allowlist: Read, Grep, Glob, Agent, TodoWrite, Skill, and the PowerShell commands `/review` and the reviewers name (`pwsh -NoProfile -File` of
  `scripts/review-scope.ps1` and `scripts/test-weakening-scan.ps1`, `Get-FileHash`, `Get-Content`, `Get-ChildItem`, `Test-Path`, `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, read-only `git`). First one
  uncounted pilot on C: read-only commands it had denied join the list, which is then fixed and recorded for every counted run.
- Order: slot 1 C then T, slot 2 T then C; n = 2 per arm. Valid, else one repeat (a second invalid run leaves that slot not settled): the result is not an error; all six reviewers were
  dispatched, each with usage and a returned message; no reviewer or parent CANNOT EXAMINE; no denied call stopped the capture, a hash check or a reviewer.
- Instrument: `grade.ps1` (sha256 `6a470f610caa`, kept beside the evidence) over the session's `subagents/`. A request's context is input + cache-creation + cache-read, counted once per API
  message id. A finding matches Dk when it is a table row in the returned message of Dk's owner, names Dk's file and matches Dk's case-insensitive pattern, frozen in the script (D4 needs
  `log` and the header or a token; D6 excludes a row that is D4's; D11 and D12 match a row opening with the DEBT id). A match by a non-owner is reported, not scored. Seen on run1's six
  reviewers (the unplanted subject): D3, D5, D6, D8, D9, D11 and D12 found, D1, D2, D4, D7 and D10 not; its context sums equal run1's table (convention-check 83,552, debt-radar 117,158).
  Every returned row is also read by hand against D1-D12; a disagreement that would change a reading makes it not settled.
- **R1**, tokens: HOLDS if, for each of the six reviewers, its mean first-request context over T's runs is at least 5,000 below its mean over C's; else FAILS.
- **R2**, findings: detect(arm, Dk) counts the arm's valid runs whose owner matched Dk. HOLDS if the sum over Dk of detect(T) is at least C's and no class's sum is two or more below C's.
  FAILS if T's sum is three or more below C's, or a class's is two or more below. Otherwise (T one or two below): slot 3 is run, C then T, and on n = 3 R2 HOLDS if T's sum is at least C's
  minus 1 and no class's is two or more below, else FAILS.
- Ship only if R1 and R2 hold and the Copilot check below reads **loads**: one guarded commit with the candidate, this measurement as its red/green evidence. Otherwise the results land,
  the candidate does not, and the entry narrows.
- Prediction, before any run. R1 HOLDS: each reviewer's first request falls by about 8,000 to 9,500 tokens (run1: 17,333 to 19,419). R2 HOLDS: C finds D3, D5, D6, D8, D9, D11 and D12 as
  run1 did, plus most plants; T is within one detection; in every T run convention-check reads `AGENTS.md`, and solid-check and test-critic the carrier. Pooled reviewer cumulative context
  falls 30% to 45%, since those three Reads add part of the chain back.
- Reported, not scored: cumulative context per reviewer and arm; each reviewer's policy Reads; returned rows; non-owner matches; the verdict; cost, wall time and denials.

every row's header names: the overlay `meta/eval-fixtures/b514-orders` is one headless `/bootstrap` (1.15 USD) whose two skill drafts this
host refused to write under `.claude/skills/` in acceptEdits, so the drafts are its denied Write payloads written byte for byte and its two
scripts were run by hand (the plan's amendment and `provenance.json`). Claude Code 2.1.312 and `claude-sonnet-5-5` in all 24 rows;
acceptEdits with the 37-rule measured list (header tag `a25d241c0177`); 24 of 24 valid, none repeated, no quota or rate-limit error;
12 invocations, one per arm and round in the registered order, 09:40 to 10:00.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| approved | 6 | 6 | 6 | 3 / 3 / 3 | 3 / 3 / 3 | 1.23 | 45 s |
| draft | 6 | 6 | 6 | 3 / 3 / 3 | 3 / 3 / 3 | 1.26 | 45 s |
| no-skill (Conventions) | 6 | 0 | 6 | 3 / 3 / 3 | 3 / 3 / 3 | 1.14 | 41 s |
| bare (no framework) | 6 | 0 | 6 | 3 / 3 / 3 | 3 / 3 / 3 | 0.78 | 33 s |

- Readings, as fixed: DRAFT-USED (6 of 6) and APPROVED-USED (6 of 6); NO-DIFFERENCE at CEILING (no-skill and bare 6 of 6); no
  CONVENTIONS-HELP. The prediction for the draft (at most 1 of 6) was wrong. In all 12 skill-arm runs the Skill call was the first tool
  call, before any read; the draft reached the model through the host's skill list (`system/init` lists both slugs), since nothing in
  `AGENTS.md` lists it. On this fixture the skill changed no outcome: every run wrote all three steps, the test row, and the raise (P1) or
  the view file (P2), and all 24 targets build (`dotnet build Orders.sln` exit 0, by hand after round 3). The skill arms cost 8 to 10% more
  and ran about 10% longer than no-skill; bare, with no framework context, was cheapest.

  first, after B-515's check. B-515: NO-DIFFERENCE at CEILING, and no run that called a draft missed a step (both drafts state every graded
  step), so this fixture cannot show a step check's value; its before-and-after needs a fixture whose instances do not show every step.
  B-356: no measured value on this shape; the decoy's false-offer rate decides alone.

As pre-registered and amended at a1d3fd07. Rows from 13:53 name 8da5842b, the records commit on top of it; the driver checked before
each run that `dist/`, `src/`, `scripts/`, `.claude/evals/` and the three overlays matched a1d3fd07. Claude Code 2.1.312 and
`claude-sonnet-5-5` in every row; acceptEdits with the 57-rule run list (`f01b98a1d7ac`); no run stopped by its cap. 36 of 36 slots
valid. The account's 5-hour usage limit stopped the series once, at 12:09 UTC after 9 valid runs; the run it cut (slot 2 S bare, one
tool call, 0.03 USD) is invalid and its registered repeat ran first after the reset (13:53 to 14:05 UTC). The scratch driver missed
that refusal's wording and made seven more attempts, each refused before the agent acted (`total_cost_usd` 0): the ERROR rows above,
not counted. Its quota check now also reads the stream's error result; on the recorded rows it stops on all 8 refusals, where the old
check stopped on none, and on none of the clean rows.

| size | arm | valid | GOOD | grader classes | hand | median USD (six runs) | median s | tool calls (median) | map read | loader read | job seen | X objects seen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S (14) | framework | 6 | 6 | CAVEATED-JOIN 6 | same | 0.155 (0.93) | 22 | 3.5 | 6 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| S (14) | bare | 6 | 0 | MISLEADING 6 | same | 0.061 (0.37) | 10 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| M (495) | framework | 6 | 6 | CAVEATED-JOIN 6 | same | 0.148 (0.89) | 21 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 2 | 3 of 3 |
| M (495) | bare | 6 | 0 | MISLEADING 4, OTHER 2 | MISLEADING 6 | 0.071 (0.43) | 11 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3 of 3 |
| L (4,999) | framework | 6 | 6 | CAVEATED-JOIN 6 | same | 0.161 (0.96) | 21 | 5 | 5 | 6 | 3 | 24 to 28 of 30 |
| L (4,999) | bare | 6 | 0 | MISLEADING 6 | same | 0.073 (0.44) | 11 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 30 of 30 |

- **Readings, applied as written.** GAP is 6 at S, M and L (6 of 6 against 0 of 6; two-sided Fisher about 0.002 at each size).
  **AT L: FRAMEWORK AHEAD AT L** (GAP_L 6). **TREND: CEILING**: GAP_S is 6, so the gap cannot widen enough to read (GAP_L - GAP_S
  = 0); AT L still applies. **COST: FALLS, NOT CROSSED**: R, the framework's median cost over the bare agent's, is 2.56 at S, 2.10 at
  M and 2.21 at L; R_L is below R_S by 13% and still above 1.0. One-off generation cost S 1.21, M 2.22, L 2.36 USD; the bare median
  is below the framework's at every size, so generation never pays for itself on cost per run.
- **Against the prediction.** H: the framework held at 6 of 6 at every size, as H said for CORRECT knowledge; but the bare agent was
  already at 0 of 6 at S, not 3 or more, so it had nowhere to fall, the gap did not widen, and the framework's cost stayed about twice
  the bare agent's at L instead of falling to it. C: the bare agent did not fall, as C said, though not for C's reason: it never searched
  for what writes `ctl.LoadRun` (0 of 18). And the framework did not fall at L: the L map was read from a subset and was still CORRECT.
  Neither prediction fits. On this scenario the framework's lead is complete and the same at 14, 495 and 4,999 files, and the bare
  agent's failure does not need size or decoys.
- **How each arm got there.** The bare agent read the DDL and joined `ctl.LoadRun` without reading the live loader (0 of 18) or a job.
  At S it drove the query from `ctl.LoadRun` (6 of 6), five times with a LEFT JOIN meant to keep runs with no sales, which returns no
  fact row because nothing writes `ctl.LoadRun`. At M it inner-joined (4) or selected from the X2 view (2). At L it inner-joined (2) or
  LEFT-joined from `ctl.LoadRun` (4), with all 30 X objects named in its tool results. The framework read `docs/warehouse-map.md` by `cat` in 16 of 18.
  The other two reached the fact from the code: M slot 3 through the loader, an X1 and a grep of `Jobs/`; L slot 5 through a grep of
  `docs/` and the views. It read the live loader in 15 of 18 and never called the `map-warehouse` skill (0 of 18). Every framework file
  is a fact-driven LEFT JOIN whose comment names the gap.
- **Hand class.** It agreed with the grader in 34 of 36. In the two M bare rows that select from `rpt.vwLoadRunRevenue`, no statement
  reads the fact, so the grader says OTHER; by hand they are MISLEADING (the view's inner join returns nothing). Both are not GOOD
  either way, so no reading changes. B-439's false red did not occur.
- **Not pooled with B-325** (Claude Code 2.1.281, `claude-sonnet-5`, the 13-file tree without the job file, an earlier framework), where the
  bare agent was 6 of 6 and the framework with its record 0 of 6. Host, model, fixture and framework all differ, and so does the direction.
- **Spend.** Runs 4.04 USD (36 valid, 4.01; the cut run, 0.03). In all 14.35 of the 60 USD stop: generation 1 4.39 (discarded),
  generation 2 5.81, two probes 0.12, runs 4.04. Each run's cost, model, host version and `durationMs` are in its row. Wall 12 to 48 s
  a run.
- **Reopen triggers** of the decisions indexed on evals, warehouse and the framework's value (WSD-016, WSD-021, WSD-027, WSD-091,
  WSD-096, WSD-097, WSD-105, WSD-107, WSD-113, WSD-122, WSD-126, WSD-127). **Met: WSD-122**, whose read-side half reopens "on B-466's
  result". That half is the scoped pass: it keeps offering rows for objects an agent only read, and keeps `CONFLICTING` beside rows it
  disagrees with. What this result bears on it: at every size the generated map was not silent on the objects the task needed, the
  agent read it and never ran the scoped pass (0 of 18), and the one sampled map, L's, was still right. So B-466 shows no case for
  changing the read side, and none of a map that misled by silence. The maintainer decides. Not met: WSD-105, which reopens B-222 to
  B-224 on an eval where captured knowledge changes a pre-registered result. Here the arms differ by the framework and its knowledge
  together; no arm isolates the knowledge, though the framework cited the map's finding in 16 of 18. WSD-113: L's bootstrap ran four
  Sonnet workers in both generations, compared with nothing. The rest name no trigger this evidence reaches.
- **Not shown:** Copilot CLI and VS Code, which both field teams use; other models, tasks and stacks; a real legacy warehouse; a
  stale, silent or wrong record (all three overlays were CORRECT); how repeatable generation is (one per size); interactive use, where
  the framework's scripts prompt instead of being refused; whether the lead grows with size on a task the bare agent passes at S.

## B-523 results, second measurement on the trap warehouse — 2026-11-15 (hand-written; the four runner rows above, 18:56 to 19:02, are the counted runs)

As amended at 9a3da48c (`.claude/plans/2026-11-15-b523-reporting-skill.md`, "Second measurement"), with the grader's weight pattern
widened twice before the pilot's reading (18c42ffd, and in this commit; both recorded in the plan). Claude Code 2.1.312 and
`claude-sonnet-5-5` in all four rows; acceptEdits with B-466's 57-rule run list (`f01b98a1d7ac`); 4 of 4 valid (exit 0, `success`,
a `.sql` written), none repeated; every run's rate-limit status was `allowed_warning`, never a refusal. The driver checked before
each run that the frozen paths matched the amendment commit the row names.

| run | arm | traps avoided (regraded) | row as written | role / semi / drill / bridge / asof / region | named / grant / manifest | Skill call | map row | cost USD | duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | C, framework today | 6 of 6, READY | FAIL, `bridge=False` | yes / yes / yes / yes / yes / yes | yes / yes / yes | none | no | 0.319 | 71.9 s |
| 2 | K, plus the skill v2 | 6 of 6, READY | FAIL, `bridge=False` | yes / yes / yes / yes / yes / yes | yes / yes / yes | `add-warehouse-report`, first call | yes | 0.323 | 66.2 s |
| 3 | C | 6 of 6, READY | FAIL, `bridge=False` | yes / yes / yes / yes / yes / yes | yes / yes / yes | none | no | 0.269 | 52.8 s |
| 4 | K | 6 of 6, READY | PASS | yes / yes / yes / yes / yes / yes | yes / yes / yes | `add-warehouse-report`, first call | yes | 0.325 | 68.9 s |

Per arm: C avoided each of the six traps in 2 of 2 runs and took all three deploy steps in 2 of 2; so did K.

- **Reading, as fixed: CEILING.** The framework as shipped today avoided all six traps in 2 of 2 runs, so the rule reads
  **NO-SHIP** and the full runs were not spent. The prediction was wrong: C did not miss the as-of segment. Both C runs joined
  `DimCustomer` on `CustomerId` with `ValidFrom <= quarter end < ValidTo`, after reading `usp_LoadDimCustomer` (run 1 cites its
  close-and-open rule), although the map's only example rule for that edge is `IsCurrent = 1`. Median cost 0.294 USD (C) and 0.324 USD (K, 1.10 times).
- **What today's framework did unprompted, both runs:**
  - It filtered posting dates by the posting-date role and took the balance at the quarter's last month end only.
  - It aggregated each fact to account grain in its own CTE, then full-outer-joined them, with a comment naming the multiplication
    it avoids.
  - It weighted both measures by the holder weight, renormalised so a joint account's shares sum to 1. It reached the region
    through `DimBranch.RegionKey` and said why `DimBranch.RegionName` was not used.
  - It put the procedure in `StoredProcedures/rpt.usp_*.sql`, with a `GRANT EXECUTE` in `Security/rpt.Permissions.sql` and a line
    at the end of `Deploy/reporting.manifest`.
  - It told the developer that holders and branches are today's, not as at the quarter.
  - It never called the `add-reporting-view` draft `/bootstrap` left (0 of 2), which covers views only.
- **What the skill added, both runs:** a written report contract in the header, and a map row (the procedure in Feeds and a dated
  Coverage line). Neither is a graded outcome.
- **Grader.** The registered weight pattern read a weight only when `*` sat directly beside `HolderWeight`. Runs 1 to 3 wrote it as
  `* COALESCE(h.HolderWeight, 1)` (runs 1 and 2), or as a renormalised `Share` column (run 3), so their rows say `bridge=False`, 5 of
  6. The hand check found all three; each fix was shown red first on a self-test case in that run's form. All four rows were regraded
  with the final grader before the reading: 6 of 6 each, which agrees with the hand check in 4 of 4. No other value differs.
  Denied calls (`denied=` 2, 1, 1, 2) were compound `cd …;` commands and heredoc writes; every denied write was redone with Write,
  Edit or `Add-Content`. No run or generation call started a sub-agent.
- **Fixture and overlay.** Building the fixture costs nothing (seeded; tree `d331b4d5e7d6…`). The generated overlay (`/bootstrap`
  1.21 USD in 2 calls, 395 s; `/map-warehouse` 0.71 USD in 2 calls, 181 s) named five of the six traps. For the as-of segment it
  leaned wrong, giving `IsCurrent = 1` as the example rule (the plan's KNOWLEDGE table).
- **Read-side.** C failed no trap, so there is no read-side failure to report. One observation, not a measured harm: on an edge
  whose only consuming view answers "now", the generated map wrote that view's `IsCurrent = 1` as the as-of rule. That follows
  `map-warehouse`'s rule 6 ("copied from a reporting view"), but it would mislead an as-at report that does not read the load.
- **Spend.** Second measurement 3.17 USD: overlay generation 1.93, four runs 1.24. With the first pilot (0.875), B-523 has spent
  4.04 USD.
- **Reopen triggers** of the decisions indexed on warehouse, skills and evals (WSD-016, WSD-020, WSD-021, WSD-027, WSD-072,
  WSD-074, WSD-091, WSD-096, WSD-097, WSD-100, WSD-105, WSD-107, WSD-109, WSD-111, WSD-113, WSD-115, WSD-122, WSD-126, WSD-127).
  **Met: WSD-127** again: the measurement does not support shipping, so the maintainer re-decides. Not met: WSD-109 and WSD-122
  reopen on field reports; WSD-107's "a measured wording that beats none" did not happen; WSD-105 needs an arm that isolates
  captured knowledge, which this run has not; WSD-113 and WSD-115 concern workers, and none started. The rest name no trigger
  this evidence reaches.
- **Not shown:** Copilot CLI and VS Code (out of scope); a reporting view on this tree (the first pilot's task was a view, on S);

## B-528 results, pilot — 2026-11-16 (hand-written; the four runner rows above, 14:58 to 15:05, are the counted runs)

As pre-registered at a1a657af (`.claude/plans/2026-11-16-b528-options.md`), unamended. One run per arm per host, in the registered
order, each from a shell with every `CLAUDE*` and `ANTHROPIC*` variable removed and `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`. Copilot CLI 1.0.98 and
`claude-sonnet-5.5` (`session.start`); Claude Code 2.1.312 and `claude-sonnet-5-5` (`system/init`), acceptEdits with the 39-rule list
(`dc735db5da74`). 4 of 4 valid as registered: exit 0, a `success` result, hooks loaded, `rails1=plan-gate`, `overlay1=True`, `railsT`
True in T and False in C. By hand, each Copilot run's first `user.message` `transformedContent` held the overlay, and in T the T
line. No repeat, no `session.error`, no quota refusal.

| run | host | arm | plan before the first write (grader; hand check agrees) | legs | security gate | cost | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Copilot | C | NEITHER: no plan at all (`doneWhen=False`); one line, "Investigating first", then the edits | 1, wrote in leg 1 | not run, and said so | 1 premium request, 26.03 AI credits | 194 s (session 172 s) |
| 2 | Copilot | T | NEITHER: no plan at all; one line, then the edits | 1, wrote in leg 1 | `security-gate` skill, two `security-auditor` calls, a High finding recorded | 1 premium request, 44.50 AI credits | 133 s (session 125 s) |
| 3 | Claude Code | C | OPTIONS, `rec=True`, leg 1: Done when, four questions, A check-then-set against B a row-version token, Recommend A | 2 | not run: read the command file, its scope capture refused by the host | 0.299 USD | 86 s |
| 4 | Claude Code | T | OPTIONS, `rec=True`, leg 1: the same two options, Recommend A | 2 | `security-gate` skill, CANNOT EXAMINE: scope capture refused by the host | 0.321 USD | 97 s |

- **The Copilot leg cannot answer the question as designed.** Copilot CLI's `-p` system message says it runs "in non-interactive
  mode" and must "not stop to ask questions or request confirmation". Both Copilot runs therefore wrote in leg 1 with no plan, so leg
  2 never ran and there was no plan to carry options or the exit, with or without the T line. Under the registered rule a full
  Copilot leg would most likely read R2-UNFIXED for a reason outside the options rule. The field's sessions waited for a reply to
  each plan, so `-p` does not reproduce them. The full Copilot run needs an amendment the maintainer decides first.
- **Claude Code:** both arms posted the design in leg 1, as B-410's T and B-412's C did on K (6 of 6 each). If the cells stay there,
  the reading is NOT REPRODUCED: on this fixture the agent follows §2 and neither R1 nor R2 is shown.
- **Security gate under the eval launch:** Claude Code's acceptEdits mode refused the gate's scope capture in both runs ("spawns a
  nested PowerShell process", ConstrainedLanguage, `$()` subexpressions), as it refused `/bootstrap`'s scripts for B-514; C never
  called the skill, T called it and stopped at CANNOT EXAMINE. So `gate` on this host measures whether the pass was started, not
  whether it completed. `dotnet test` was blocked by this machine's Application Control policy in three of four runs; no plan grade
  depends on it. In the T arm the patched router shows as a modified file in `git status` (the runner's patch adds no commit), and
  Copilot run 2 mentioned it.
- **Rate limit:** every Claude Code stream carried `rate_limit_event` `allowed_warning`, seven-day window at 89%, resetting
  2026-11-18 11:00 UTC; not a stop as registered.
- **Counts toward n:** as registered, each run is slot 1 of its cell. An amended Copilot launch would make runs 1 and 2 not count.
- **Projected full run**, from these four: Claude Code, 10 more runs at about 0.31 USD and 90 s each, about 3.1 USD and 15 minutes,
  inside the seven-day window's last 11%. Copilot as registered: 10 more runs at 1 premium request and 26 to 45 AI credits each,
  about 10 requests, 350 credits and 30 minutes, but measuring the `-p` instruction rather than the options rule. A two-leg Copilot design
  that stops for a plan would cost about 2 premium requests a run.
- **Reopen triggers checked:** WSD-100 (keep `route-prompt`), WSD-111 (the security-pass wording) and WSD-114 (the `security-gate`
  name): none met. No run sent the pass to a host built-in.
- Pilot spend: 0.621 USD on Claude Code; 2 premium requests and 70.53 AI credits on Copilot.
